name: Early Lake Turkana pastoralism
description: Communities near Lake Turkana combined herding domestic animals with fishing during the early Pastoral Neolithic.

impact.note: The arrival of herding in eastern Africa gave regional communities a new livelihood that later pastoral societies there continued.

date.label: Approximately 5000 years BP (3050 BCE)
date.basis: Source-reported period or approximate chronology; where calibrated BP is stated, converted using the 1950 reference epoch.

events.statement: Communities near Lake Turkana combined herding domestic animals with fishing during the early Pastoral Neolithic.
events.caveats: The date is a broad regional approximation rather than a dated first adoption event; genetic, archaeological and cultural pathways of herding transmission are incompletely resolved.

evidence.supports: The review of archaeological evidence describes herding and fishing near Lake Turkana at the beginning of the Pastoral Neolithic around 5000 BP.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest source-supported dated event for this scoped record; not a global priority claim.
